categories.main_business_segments: ZoomInfo is a global leader in modern go-to-market software, data, and intelligence for sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting teams. The company operates through RevOS, its cloud-based operating system for revenue professionals, organized into four main product suites: SalesOS (sales engagement and call recording), MarketingOS (marketing automation and lead generation), OperationsOS (data operations and enrichment), and TalentOS (recruiting and talent acquisition). The company also offers ZoomInfo Lite, a free community edition.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: ZoomInfo leverages an AI and machine learning-powered data engine that aggregates data from millions of sources, standardizes and matches data to entities, verifies accuracy, and applies processed data at scale. The platform operates across three layers: an Intelligence Layer (billions of data points about companies and contacts), an Orchestration Layer (data integration and workflow automation), and an Engagement Layer (multi-channel communication tools). The company employs a human-in-the-loop approach combining proprietary algorithms with research analysts and data scientists to ensure data quality and maintain a contractual guarantee of at least 95% accuracy on certain data points.
categories.primary_customers_markets: ZoomInfo serves over 35,000 companies across diverse industry verticals, with the top five industries being software (33% of ACV), non-IT business services (18%), IT services (10%), financial/insurance/real estate (8%), and manufacturing (5%). Customers range from large global enterprises to mid-market and small businesses, with 1,820 customers contracting for over $100,000 in ACV as of December 31, 2023. No single customer contributed more than 1% of revenue in 2023. Approximately 13% of revenue comes from customers outside the United States.
categories.geographic_coverage: ZoomInfo operates globally with corporate headquarters in Vancouver, Washington, and additional offices in Waltham, Massachusetts; Bethesda, Maryland; Conshohocken, Pennsylvania; Grand Rapids, Michigan; San Francisco, California; Ra'anana, Israel; Toronto, Canada; Chennai, India; and London, England. The company has 74% of employees in North America, 12% in the Middle East, 12% in Asia, 2% in Europe, and less than 1% in Australia. International revenues accounted for approximately 13% of total revenue in 2023.
categories.supply_chain_position: ZoomInfo operates in the downstream segment of the go-to-market technology supply chain, providing end-user software, data, and intelligence solutions directly to sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting professionals. The company does not manufacture physical products but delivers cloud-based SaaS services. Infrastructure is hosted through third-party data centers operated by Google and Amazon Web Services. The company integrates with major CRM systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics, and Oracle Sales Cloud.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: ZoomInfo's strategic priorities include expanding its AI and machine learning capabilities, particularly in generative AI applications. The company is investing in developing new features and functionality across its four product suites (SalesOS, MarketingOS, OperationsOS, TalentOS) to drive incremental customer value. R&D initiatives focus on enhancing data accuracy and coverage, improving platform integrations with third-party systems, and expanding internationally. The company also pursues selective acquisitions to complement and expand platform capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: ZoomInfo generates substantially all revenue from subscription services to its cloud-based platform, with subscriptions typically ranging from one to three years. Over 45% of customer contracts are multi-year agreements. The company bills customers in advance on an annual, semi-annual, or quarterly basis and recognizes subscription revenue ratably over the contract term. Additional revenue comes from recurring usage-based services and professional services fees. Pricing is based on functionality provided, number of users, and amount of data integrated into customer systems.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: ZoomInfo competes in a rapidly evolving, highly competitive market with low barriers to entry. Primary competitors include LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Dun & Bradstreet Hoovers, and TechTarget, as well as free online sources and customers' internal databases. The company also faces potential competition from larger, well-funded companies in adjacent markets such as CRM (Salesforce, Oracle), business software (Microsoft), and advertising (Google). ZoomInfo differentiates through comprehensive platform offering, data quality and accuracy, breadth and depth of data coverage, ease of use, integration capabilities, and tangible ROI for customers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: ZoomInfo is a large accelerated filer with significant financial scale. For the year ended December 31, 2023, the company generated revenue of $1,239.5 million (compared to $1,098.0 million in 2022), representing 12.9% year-over-year growth. GAAP operating income was $259.5 million (21% margin) in 2023 versus $175.8 million (16% margin) in 2022. GAAP net income was $107.3 million in 2023 versus $63.2 million in 2022. The company had 3,516 employees as of December 31, 2023. Market capitalization was approximately $8.7 billion as of June 30, 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: ZoomInfo's core value proposition is enabling sales, marketing, operations, and recruiting professionals to shorten sales cycles and increase win rates by delivering the right message to the right person at the right time. Key differentiators include: comprehensive platform covering multiple go-to-market functions; best-in-class data accuracy with contractual 95% guarantee; billions of data points from first- and third-party sources; AI/ML-powered data engine with human-in-the-loop quality assurance; seamless integration with major CRM and business systems; and a contributory network that continuously improves data quality. The company's RevOS operating system provides a unified, integrated approach to go-to-market intelligence and execution.
